standard_prerequisites.name: A prime of the larger ring minimal over the image of a prime of the smaller one lies over a minimal prime, and the unique point over the generic point of the spectrum of the smaller domain is the generic point
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the unique point mapping to the generic point with the zero ideal, which is what makes the fibre a field-like ring with a single prime.

standard_prerequisites.name: A flat local ring homomorphism is faithfully flat, so a flat map of domains is injective, and an element of the larger ring that maps to a unit of the fibre after localizing is a unit there
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the element b' and the exponent giving an element of the smaller ring that lies in the ideal.

standard_prerequisites.name: Integral, quasi-finite, unramified and etale ring maps have no nontrivial specializations between points of fibres
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the seven hypotheses to case (7), so that only one case has to be proved directly.

core_obligations: Prove case (7): if exactly one point of the larger spectrum maps to the generic point, then that point is the zero ideal; take a nonzero b in the ideal J, observe that b becomes a unit in the fibre over the generic point, invoke the unit criterion and the description of that fibre as a filtered colimit of localizations to find a nonzero f of the smaller ring such that b becomes a unit after inverting f, and conclude that a power of f lies in J (proof lines 31720-31736).

Show that case (6) implies case (7): the generic point of the larger spectrum maps to the generic point of the smaller one, so under case (6) it is the unique point doing so (proof lines 31744-31748).

Show that cases (1) to (5) imply case (6): under each of them the map is flat, hence injective, so the generic point of the larger spectrum maps to the generic point, and the absence of nontrivial specializations between points of fibres is exactly the remaining condition (proof lines 31740-31751).

Verify the absence of nontrivial specializations from the sources cited for the integral, quasi-finite, unramified and etale cases, which completes the reduction of all seven hypotheses to case (7) (proof lines 31752-31759).
proof_roadmap: Prove case (7) by turning a nonzero element of the ideal into a unit of the fibre at the generic point and clearing denominators (proof lines 31720-31736).
Deduce case (7) from case (6) by the uniqueness of the point over the generic point (proof lines 31744-31748).
Deduce case (6) from cases (1) to (5) using flatness for injectivity and the cited absence of specializations (proof lines 31740-31759).
difficulty_reason: The statement gives seven different hypotheses on a map of domains, one of them purely topological about specializations between points of fibres, and concludes that every nonzero ideal of the target meets the source in a nonzero element (statement lines 31701-31718). The proof does not treat the seven cases separately: it proves the last one, where exactly one point of the larger spectrum maps to the generic point, by showing that a nonzero element of the ideal becomes a unit over the generic point and then descending to a localization of the source so that a power of a nonzero element lies in the ideal, and then reduces the other six cases to it through flatness for injectivity and the absence of nontrivial specializations for the integral, quasi-finite, unramified and etale cases (proof lines 31720-31759). The reduction structure is what makes the statement usable, and the denominators argument in off case (7) is its technical core. The counted span refers seven times to labelled results of other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.
